ambiguities.description: Open ambiguities this step could not settle; each names what it is about. An item is deleted once its answer is applied.

milestones.description: List of design milestones: named groups of the upstream nodes a delivery slice schedules. Milestones are listed in ascending target_date order (E520 otherwise); the order states no dependency, and a milestone names no predecessor.

milestone_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier. Recommended format: milestone-{phase}-{description}. Example: 'milestone-phase1-user-auth'. Should be stable: changing it breaks the references to this milestone.

name.description: Human-readable name of the milestone, distinguishable from all other milestones in this plan. Use Title Case, 3–6 words describing the major deliverable or theme. Examples: 'Core Authentication API', 'Payment Integration', 'User Profile Management', 'Performance Hardening', 'Data Migration Phase 1'. Avoid sequential labels ('Milestone 1', 'Phase A') — they carry no semantic meaning and make roadmap reports unreadable. Avoid implementation verbs ('Implement Auth', 'Build Payment') — use noun phrases describing the delivered capability.

target_date.description: Target completion date for this milestone in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Example: '2025-03-31'. Should align with team sprint boundaries or external deadlines where applicable. Anti-pattern: relative dates ('end of Q1', 'in 6 weeks') — always convert to absolute YYYY-MM-DD dates for deterministic tooling.

risks.description: Known risks that could delay or block this milestone from completing on time. Each risk should identify the source, potential impact, and the work it affects. Example: 'Third-party OAuth provider SLA instability may delay auth milestone by 2 weeks — monitor weekly, escalate if 2 consecutive missed SLAs'. Format: '{risk source} may {impact} — {mitigation/monitoring action}'. Anti-pattern: 'External dependencies' (too vague) or listing a risk without a mitigation or monitoring action. Write no node id into the text.

spikes.description: Technical spikes or investigations required before implementation work can proceed. List each spike as a time-boxed question to be answered. Examples: 'Can PostgreSQL handle 10k concurrent connections with our current schema? (2-day spike before the infrastructure work)', 'Does the third-party API rate limit apply per IP or per account? (1-day spike before the integration work)'. Format: '{question to answer} ({time-box} before {the work it unblocks})'. Write no node id into the text. Anti-pattern: listing implementation tasks as spikes — spikes are for unknown unknowns only.

schedules.description: Ids of the nodes this milestone schedules: functional requirements or acceptance criteria, APIs, invariants, NFRs, components, environments and charter risks. At least one. The capability a milestone serves is computed from the functional requirements it schedules. Example: ["fr-password-reset", "risk-reset-link-takeover"]. Anti-pattern: listing another milestone (milestone order is not stored) or a free-text deliverable.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this milestone: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former ids of this milestone; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

derives_from.description: Ids of the seeds this design milestone takes content from directly. Optional: list a seed routed to this step, and only for content taken straight from the seed and not through an upstream node.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this milestone replaces. Optional.

items.description: A single design milestone: a name, an optional target date, the nodes it schedules, and its risks and spikes.

migration_plan.description: High-level strategy for migrating from existing systems. Required only when this implementation plan replaces existing data schemas, replaces a running system, or changes a public API contract in a breaking way. Describe in 2–4 sentences covering: (1) the migration sequence (dual-write, cutover) and (2) the rollback mechanism (guidance, not checked: no keyword or tool enforces the length). What is replaced is stated by links, not here: `replaces` on the node that takes the place of a deleted one, and the `removes` of a removal task criterion. What confirms the migration is a task criterion of step 14 with a verifier in `verified_by`, not a sentence here. No tool reads a link out of this string: a node id written in it is not a link. Example: 'Existing user records move from PostgreSQL 12 to 15 using pg_upgrade. Writes go to both databases for a 48-hour dual-write period, then reads cut over to the new one. Rollback by restoring the pre-migration snapshot within 4 hours.' Omit if no migration is required.

environment_ref.description: Canonical reference to the deployment environment required for this milestone. Kind must be 'environment'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:environment:staging", "kind": "environment", "label": "staging"}. Common IDs: 'cn:core:environment:dev', 'cn:core:environment:staging', 'cn:core:environment:prod'. Use to indicate which environment this milestone targets for delivery or testing.

allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).
